## Historical audit — S0256

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/audit_sources/raw_failures/scene_rsi_v2_1/r1/fixed_h0/H0/selection/commons_194983350/trajectory.jsonl`. All citations below refer to this file; character ranges cover the supplied complete line observations.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1, [0,5615) | The formal goal was to reconstruct a 342 × 512 indoor photograph as separate 3D meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, placement and materials, without using the reference as a texture. The image itself is not visible in this audit. |
| Student response and execution, lines 3 [0,10340), 4 [0,10982) | The student wrote and the runner attempted a nonempty program for a scene named “Colorful cafe.” It specifies multiple objects: architecture, shelving and plants, a banquette and cushions, tables, chairs, counter and ceiling tiles. These names and code express the student's interpretation, not independent confirmation of the photograph. |
| Student code, line 3 [0,10340) | Colored primitives, roughness and sheen settings, upholstery marks, and geometric patches intended to suggest mottled glass provide material/detail approximations; no image texture is specified. The code groups sofa, table and chair components and positions legs and supports, but grouping does not verify physical connection or visual alignment. Chair orientation and other object poses are specified, not validated. |
| Student code, line 3 [0,10340) | The program sets a camera, three area lights, world illumination, Cycles and 48 samples. Framing, illumination, occlusion and render quality cannot be checked from code alone. |
| Student session, line 2 [0,2858); result, line 5 [0,1080) | One observable student CLI turn had zero tool calls. The sole recorded execution timed out after approximately 316 seconds, with empty stdout/stderr and a null image. No rendered review, revision, successful build, or `DONE` is recorded. The timeout does not identify whether geometry construction, rendering, or another stage caused the delay. |

**Teacher and exploration:** No teacher input, detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or adoption is recorded in this student trajectory. The student produced its own single candidate; no separate exploratory tool use or iterative visual comparison is visible.

**Outcome:** Technical interruption on the first recorded execution; reconstruction correctness and final submission outcome are unknown. This is not an empty patch or evidence of an algorithmic failure. Neither the scene name nor the amount of modeled detail verifies similarity to the unseen reference.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** Transferably, a runnable-looking scene specification and object grouping require successful execution and visual checks before claims about connections, pose, materials or camera matching. Here, the many generated components and rendering settings are task-specific possible contributors to runtime, but their causal role remains an unresolved hypothesis. No render or reference image is available to assess whether any particular object, lighting choice or framing is correct.
